---
title: "RMS amplitude semantics"
---

`audio.lowlevel.rms` and its `audio.rms` alias return the square root of the mean
squared **raw samples** in each frame. A constant-amplitude0.2 signal therefore
returns0.2. Frame positions and the existing right-zero-padding policy for inputs
shorter than one frame are unchanged. Multiple channels are averaged first, as
in the existing audio frontend.

The earlier implementation accidentally reused Hann-tapered FFT frames. For
stationary inputs that reduced amplitude by approximately `sqrt(3/8)`; for
transients it also changed the result with position inside a frame. A constant
scale correction cannot repair that transient weighting.

The corrected extractor catalog version is1.1 and metadata records
`code_version="rms-untapered-v2"` and `windowing="rectangular"`. These identities
invalidate cached results computed with the old semantics. Existing saved
outputs are not rewritten: downstream comparisons should pin their original
source or explicitly re-extract a separately versioned result.

FFT/STFT features continue to use their periodic Hann taper. Tests independently
check this unchanged frontend alongside constant/sinusoid/impulse/gain and
native-time RMS behavior.
